FORBES: "Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum Cruelly Acts Like The U.S. Is A Neighbor"
June 1, 2026 | 🤡

📰 John Tamny's grievance, no joke: Sheinbaum denied Sempra's Sinaloa LNG terminal and cancelled Royal Caribbean's $1B Mahahual cruise port. Mexico choosing what gets built on its own coast is now "cruelty" toward the United States.

🇲🇽 What Forbes leaves out: Mahahual borders the second-largest reef on the planet. The Sempra LNG was opposed by Sinaloa communities for years. The columnist's actual complaint is that Mexicans get a vote.

• Sheinbaum acts "cruelly" by treating U.S. like a neighbor
• Mexican presidents "operate fully aware that the U.S. economy will always protect them from themselves"

🇲🇽📉 MEXICAN INFLATION COOLS TO 4.11% — ENERGY PRICES DROP 1.64% AS CFE SUMMER TARIFFS KICK IN

INEGI: annual inflation eased to 4.11% in the first half of May 2026, down from 4.45% at April's close. The non-core index fell 1.14% biweekly, driven by a 1.64% drop in energy and government-authorized tariffs — including CFE's summer electricity adjustments across 11 cities. Core inflation steady at 4.22%. Banxico is holding its policy rate "por cierto tiempo" to anchor the path toward its 3% target by mid-2027. While US PCE inflation hit a 3-year high of 3.8% and Powell's Fed gets squeezed by Trump, Mexico's monetary sovereignty plays out: disinflation without the social wreckage of a shock cycle.

Source: El Economista / INEGI

🇲🇽⚽ MEXICO'S FINTECH HARDENS FOR WORLD CUP — MERCADO PAGO LAUNCHES "ARMORED MODE"

Mercado Pago rolled out Modo Blindado ahead of the 2026 World Cup: geolocated safe-zone authentication, hidden balances and reduced transfer limits outside trusted networks, real-time fraud algorithms monitoring thousands of variables per second. Spokesperson Ramiro Nández: "Queremos que nuestros usuarios salgan con la certeza de que, pase lo que pase, su dinero está siempre protegido." 7 of 10 surveyed users said they'd activate immediately. Mexico is hosting the inauguration plus 13 World Cup matches — and its private financial infrastructure is preparing harder than the gringo press is willing to admit.

Source: regeneracion.mx

🚨🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM: TWO FOREIGN AGENTS DIED IN UNAUTHORIZED FIELD OP IN CHIHUAHUA

Not persecution — sovereignty. The Maru Campos investigation centers on the April 19 drug-lab raid in Sierra Tarahumara that left four dead: two state prosecutors and two foreign agents whose presence on Mexican soil was never authorized. Sheinbaum: "¿Por qué había dos personas extranjeras en una operación en campo? Se colabora y se coordina, pero no puede haber operativos en tierra conjuntos." Mexican law requires foreign agents to register with SRE and bars joint field operations. Ex-Chihuahua prosecutor César Jáuregui already resigned. The FGR wants to know who authorized US boots on Mexican ground.

Source: contralinea.com.mx

🔥🇲🇽 9 CFE OFFICIALS EARN MORE THAN PRESIDENT SHEINBAUM — IN VIOLATION OF THE CONSTITUTION

Contralínea investigation: CFE director Emilia Calleja takes home 214,716 pesos/month — 1.61x Sheinbaum's 133,332. Her own secretary, Diana López Piña, pulls 287,406. Eight more CFE executives — including legal director José Manuel Calva (242,438) and HR subdirector Cecilia Braña (232,924) — breach Article 127's constitutional cap. Public payroll portals report fake lower numbers; internal CFE documents revealed the real figures. CFE has refused to answer since April. The neoliberal apparatus 4T inherited is still skimming the people's electricity company from the inside.

Source: contralinea.com.mx

🚨🇲🇽 NEWARK IMPOSES CURFEW AROUND ICE BLACK SITE — DETAINEE HUNGER STRIKE ENTERS 2ND WEEK

Mayor Ras Baraka declared a 9pm–6am curfew in a half-mile radius around Delaney Hall after a week of clashes between protesters and federal agents. Inside, around 300 of the facility's 1,000 detainees are on hunger strike denouncing expired food, denied medical care, and abuse. Delaney Hall was the first ICE center opened under Trump's second term — a 15-year, $1 billion GEO Group contract. Newark just declared its own streets a curfew zone to protect a private prison holding migrants without charge.

Source: jornada.com.mx

🚨🌎 COLOMBIA'S FAR-RIGHT TAKES FIRST ROUND — REGIONAL PROGRESSIVE BLOC TESTED

Milei-aligned outsider Abelardo de la Espriella took 43.74% (10.36M votes) Sunday, edging Pacto Histórico's Iván Cepeda (40.90%, 9.69M). VOX's Abascal and Ecuador's Noboa congratulated De la Espriella the same night. June 21 second round will decide. The Latin American right is networking openly — and the regional bloc Sheinbaum, Lula and Petro have been holding together just got its hardest test in a year.

Source: jornada.com.mx

🇲🇽🏭 <u>RECORD $4.52B APRIL SURPLUS — EXPORTS UP 32.6%, NON-AUTO MANUFACTURING +45.8%</u>

Mexico's trade surplus hit $4.520 billion in April, ~10x the $476 million Bloomberg consensus, El Financiero reports. Exports reached $72.042 billion — the highest single-month figure since INEGI began records in 1980 — pulled by non-automotive manufacturing growth of 45.8% annual. Jan–April surplus stands at $3.508 billion, against a $314 million deficit in the same period of 2025. The US absorbed 83.6% of those exports. Trump's tariff wall is not delivering what was advertised.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX DEBT DOWN $20B, 1.3M BARRELS/DAY — MEXICO'S FUEL HOLDS WHILE WORLD BURNS</u>

Sheinbaum, defending the Olmeca/Dos Bocas refinery, the Deer Park purchase in Texas, and the rebuilt coker units at Tula and Salina Cruz: "We rescued Pemex and CFE as true companies of the people." Pemex has cut $20 billion in debt while processing 1.3 million barrels per day. CFE has added 3,000 MW from six new combined-cycle plants since the sexenio began, with 32,000 MW more queued and renewables programmed to climb from 24% to 38%. While oil markets convulse over Hormuz, Mexican families pay yesterday's price for gasoline and diesel.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>US IS 100% IMPORT-DEPENDENT ON MEXICO FOR 3 CRITICAL MINERALS</u>

Mexico produces over 60 minerals. Nine are on Trump's "critical" list. The US depends on Mexico for 100% of its fluorite, graphite, and strontium imports — plus 77% of silver, 75%+ of barite, 73% of zinc, 57% of refined copper. Trump's "Pax Silica" framework gathered 54 countries on February 4 to lock down supply chains against China; the US Eximbank put up $10 billion for the Vault Project and another $14.8 billion in Letters of Interest. The mineral war is on, and Mexico holds cards Washington needs.
